questions.question: Which living organism has the longest scientifically documented lifespan?
questions.hint: One specimen, nicknamed 'Ming,' was determined to be approximately 507 years old, making it one of the longest-lived known animals.

questions.question: Which desert receives the lowest average annual rainfall?
questions.hint: Although the Atacama has places that receive virtually no rain, Antarctica has the lowest average annual precipitation, qualifying it as the driest desert overall.

questions.question: Which movie was the first feature-length animated film ever released?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.hint: Released in 1937, Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was the first full-length cel-animated feature film.

questions.question: Which fictional archaeologist is the main protagonist of the Tomb Raider franchise?
questions.hint: Lara Croft debuted in 1996 and became one of the most recognizable video game and film characters.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the annual World Press Freedom Index?
questions.hint: The World Press Freedom Index ranks countries based on the level of freedom available to journalists.

questions.question: Which international organization sets global standards for measurement through the International System of Units (SI)?
questions.hint: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) oversees the SI system used worldwide.

questions.question: Which civilization built the ancient city of Troy, according to archaeological evidence?
questions.hint: Archaeological evidence suggests Troy was an Anatolian city with connections to the Hittite world, rather than being founded by the later Greeks of legend.

questions.question: Which treaty officially created the European Union?
questions.hint: Signed in 1992, the Maastricht Treaty formally established the European Union.

questions.question: Which country has won the most Olympic gold medals in women's gymnastics?
questions.hint: The Soviet Union dominated women's artistic gymnastics during much of the 20th century.

questions.question: Which Grand Slam tournament is played on clay courts?
questions.hint: The French Open at Roland Garros is the only Grand Slam played on clay.

questions.question: Which country has the greatest number of volcanoes?
questions.hint: Indonesia has the largest number of active volcanoes due to its location on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

questions.question: Which nation is the world's largest archipelago by number of islands?
questions.hint: Indonesia consists of more than 17,000 islands, making it the world's largest archipelagic state.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the laws of planetary motion that describe elliptical orbits?
questions.hint: Kepler's three laws accurately describe how planets orbit the Sun.

questions.question: Which SI base unit measures the amount of substance?
questions.hint: The mole is one of the seven SI base units and measures the amount of substance.

questions.question: Which civilization constructed the cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde?
questions.hint: Mesa Verde National Park preserves remarkable cliff dwellings built by the Ancestral Pueblo people.

questions.question: Which language family has the greatest number of native speakers worldwide?
questions.hint: The Indo-European language family includes English, Spanish, Hindi, Portuguese, Russian, and many other widely spoken languages.

questions.question: Which mammal has the slowest heartbeat?
questions.hint: A blue whale's heart can beat as slowly as 2 beats per minute during deep dives.

questions.question: Which country has the highest number of official languages at the national level?
questions.hint: Bolivia recognizes 37 official languages, including Spanish and numerous Indigenous languages.

questions.question: Which scientist discovered the expanding universe through observations of distant galaxies?
questions.hint: Edwin Hubble's observations showed that galaxies are moving away from each other, providing key evidence for an expanding universe. Georges Lemaître independently developed the theoretical interpretation.

questions.question: Which empire built the extensive road network known as the Royal Road?
questions.hint: The Royal Road stretched approximately 2,700 km (1,700 miles) and enabled rapid communication across the Achaemenid Empire.
